title: Rotate List
interviewTips: Clarify: can k be larger than list length? Yes, up to 2e9, so ask if you should use k % n.
Trade-off: repeated single-step rotation is simple but O(n*k); closing the list into a ring achieves O(n) in one pass.
Edge-case tip: handle empty list, single node, k==0, and k % n == 0 early; ensure you break the circle to avoid cycles.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Single-Step Rotation
approaches.intuition: Rotating right by 1 means moving the last node to the front. Repeat this operation k times to get rotation by k. Use modulo to avoid useless full cycles.
approaches.theory: For each of k_eff = k % n rotations, traverse to find tail and its predecessor prev. Detach tail via prev.next = None and prepend it via tail.next = head. After k_eff iterations the head points to the rotated list. Each iteration costs O(n) traversal, total O(n * k_eff).

timeComplexity.explanation: Compute length in O(n), then up to k % n rotations each scanning O(n) to find tail. Worst case O(n^2) when k % n ~ n.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only a few pointers prev, cur, tail are used, no extra allocation.

steps: iter1: find tail 5, prev 4, move 5 to front -> [5,1,2,3,4]
iter2: find tail 4, prev 3, move 4 to front -> [4,5,1,2,3]

edgeCases: Empty list or single node: return head directly
k == 0 or k % n == 0: no rotation needed
k >> n e.g. [0,1,2], k=4: modulo reduces to 1 rotation

approaches.name: Approach 2: Close Into Ring and Break
approaches.intuition: Right rotation by k moves the last k nodes to front. If we connect tail to head to form a circle, the new head is n-k steps from old head and new tail is just before it. Cut the circle there.
approaches.theory: Traverse once to get length n and tail. Link tail.next = head to make circular list. Let k %= n. If k==0 break circle and return. Otherwise newTail is at position n-k-1 from head (0-indexed), newHead = newTail.next. Set newTail.next = None to break ring. This is one pass O(n) and uses two-pointer walk to the break point.

timeComplexity.explanation: One traversal to find length and tail O(n), plus walk of n-k-1 steps to new tail O(n). Total linear.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only pointers tail, newTail, newHead are used, in-place relinking.

steps: Traverse: n=5, tail=5, link 5->1 to form circle: 1->2->3->4->5->1...
k% n =2, need newTail at n-k-1=2 steps from head: 1->2->3, so newTail=3

edgeCases: head null or single node: return head
k % n == 0: must break circle before return to avoid cycle
n-k-1 == 0 when newTail is old head, e.g. [1,2], k=1 -> [2,1]
